content.title: How to watch Timberwolves at Pistons tonight: game preview, injury updates and TV and streaming info | Minnesota Timberwolves
content.text: The Minnesota Timberwolves are back in action Thursday with a road matchup against the Pistons in Detroit.Minnesota is coming off a dominant 124–94 win over the Dallas Mavericks on Monday. The victory was highlighted by the return of Anthony Edwards, who finished with 17 points, and a triple-double from Ayo Dosunmu, who recorded 18 points, 15 rebounds and 12 assists.Sixth in the West at 46–29, the Wolves are 6–4 over their last 10 games and 21–15 on the road. Minnesota currently ranks fifth in the league in defense (111.9 defensive rating) and 12th in offense (115.5 offensive rating).Here is your full guide to Thursday’s Timberwolves at Pistons matchup, including injury news and how to watch live.How to watch, stream & listen to Timberwolves at PistonsDate: Thursday, April 2Start Time: 6 PM CTTV Channel/Live Stream: FanDuel Sports Network | Prime VideoRadio: iHeartRadio | Timberwolves app Where: Little Caesars Arena | Detroit, MIWolves at Pistons tips off at 6 PM on Thursday, April 2 from Little Caesars Arena in Detroit. The game will be broadcast and streamed on FanDuel Sports Network and Prime Video.Injury ReportNote: Tonight's injury report will be updated before the start of the game.Timberwolves Out: Anthony Edwards, Jaden McDaniels, Enrique Freeman, Zyon Pullin and Rocco ZikarskyAnthony Edwards (Right Knee; Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome; Illness), Jaden McDaniels (Left Knee; Patella Tendinopathy), Enrique Freeman (G League-Two-Way), Zyon Pullin (G League-Two-Way) and Rocco Zikarsky (G League-Two-Way) are out.PistonsQuestionable: Marcus SasserOut: Cade Cunningham & Isaiah Stewart Marcus Sasser (Right Hip Strain) is questionable to play. Cade Cunningham (Left Lung; Pneumothorax) and Isaiah Stewart (Left Calf; Strain) are out.Jerseys Timberwolves: Association EditionPistons: Statement EditionThe Wolves will be in their white Association Edition uniforms against the Pistons, who will be in their black Statement Edition uniforms.What to know about the PistonsFirst in the East at 55–21, Detroit enters Thursday’s matchup following a 127–116 win over Toronto on Tuesday. The Pistons rank second in the league in defense (108.8 defensive rating) and ninth in offense (116.9 offensive rating).Thurday marks the second and final matchup between Detroit and Minnesota this season. The Pistons lead the season series 1-0.With star guard Cade Cunningham and forward Isaiah Stewart sidelined, Detroit will continue to lean on big man Jalen Duren. The starting group also features Kevin Huerter, Tobias Harris, Ausar Thompson, and Daniss Jenkins. Despite the injuries to Cunningham and Stewart, the Pistons have remained elite, winning seven of their last 10 games to maintain the top seed in the Eastern Conference.
